## 0.2 Define generic functions
```{r setup2}
# Helper function to quote arguments (similar to Perl's qw)
qw <- function(...) {
  sapply(match.call()[-1], deparse)
}

# Create an empty data frame with specified dimensions and column names
createEmptyDf = function( nrow, ncol, colnames = c() ){
  data.frame( matrix( vector(), nrow, ncol, dimnames = list( c(), colnames ) ) )
}

# Generate a distance dataframe from a distance matrix and a label
make_dist_dataframe<-function(fn_dist,fn_name){ # distance matrix, name tag
  fn_cbs<-attr(fn_dist, "Labels") # Extract labels from the distance matrix
  fn_cbpairs<-carbon_pairs %>% select(carbon1,carbon2,key) # Select key columns from the reference carbon_pairs dataframe
  fn_tmp1<-dist_long(fn_dist) # Transform distance matrix to long format
  fn_tmp2<-data.frame(rows=fn_cbs,cols=fn_cbs,distance=0) # Create self-to-self distance (distance = 0)
  fn_tmp3<-fn_tmp1 %>% select(cols,rows,distance) %>% rename(rows="cols",cols="rows") # Create mirrored pairs to ensure bidirectional coverage
  fn_tmp<-bind_rows(fn_tmp1,fn_tmp2,fn_tmp3) # Combine all distance entries
  # fn_tmp<-bind_rows(fn_tmp,fn_tmp3) # Combine all distance entries
  colnames(fn_tmp)<-c("carbon1","carbon2",paste("dist",fn_name,sep="_"))
  fn_cbpairs<-left_join(fn_cbpairs,fn_tmp,by=c("carbon1","carbon2")) # Join with the reference dataframe
  return(fn_cbpairs)
}

# Generate ggplot2-style colors using HCL scales
ggColorHue <- function(n, l=65) {
  hues <- seq(15, 375, length=n+1)
  hcl(h=hues, l=l, c=100)[1:n]
}

# Calculate distance based on Spearman's rank correlation (1 - rho)
spearman_dist <- function(x) {
  # Use 1 - correlation as distance
  as.dist(1 - cor(x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
}

Sys.time()
```

# 1 Carbon sources
## 1.1 Load carbon source metadata and define categories
```{r Carbon1}
# Define metabolic categories
carbon_categories<-c("Upper Glycolysis","Lower Glycolysis","Pentose Phosphate","TCA cycle","Entner Doudoroff","Amino acid-derived TCA input")
# Load carbon source mapping (Abbreviations and Categories)
carbon_names<-paste(getwd(),"Carbon_Info","Carbon_name.csv",sep="/") %>% read_csv()
# Assign colors to each metabolic category using a named vector for efficiency
category_colors <- c(
  "Upper Glycolysis" = "#0072B2",
  "Lower Glycolysis" = "#E69F00",
  "Pentose Phosphate" = "#56B4E9",
  "TCA cycle" = "#009E73",
  "Entner Doudoroff" = "#CC79A7",
  "Amino acid-derived TCA input" = "#8FD926"
)

# Map category colors back to the main dataframe
carbon_names$Category_col <- category_colors[carbon_names$Category]

# Generate all possible carbon source pairs for matrix operations
# upper triangle (pairwise combinations)
df_upper <- combn(carbon_names$Abb, 2) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
colnames(df_upper) <- qw(carbon1, carbon2)
df_upper$key <- "upper"

# diagonal (self-to-self)
df_diag <- data.frame(carbon1 = carbon_names$Abb, carbon2 = carbon_names$Abb, key = "diag")

# lower triangle (mirrored)
df_lower <- df_upper %>% rename(carbon1 = "carbon2", carbon2 = "carbon1")
df_lower$key <- "lower"

# Combine into a comprehensive pairs dataframe
carbon_pairs_pre <- bind_rows(df_upper, df_diag, df_lower)

# Join category information for both carbons in a pair
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  left_join(carbon_names %>% select(carbon1 = Abb, category1 = Category), by = "carbon1") %>%
  left_join(carbon_names %>% select(carbon2 = Abb, category2 = Category), by = "carbon2")

# Determine if the pair belongs to the same category or is a "between-category" pair
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  mutate(pair_category = ifelse(category1 == category2, category1, "between"))

# Assign colors to the pair categories
carbon_pairs_pre <- carbon_pairs_pre %>%
  left_join(
    data.frame(pair_category = c(names(category_colors), "between"),
               category_col = c(as.character(category_colors), "black")),
    by = "pair_category"
  )

Sys.time()
```
## 1.2 Load essential reactions defined by genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs)
```{r carbon2, fig.height=8,fig.width=10, dpi=300}
# Function to read essential reaction data and calculate pairwise distances
calculate_gem_distances <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load mapping for carbon abbreviations
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA","growth_media", "Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load essential reaction list for the specific strain
  ess_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join with mapping and filter out unassigned carbons
  ess_data <- ess_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Identify unique reactions and carbons
  unique_reactions <- unique(ess_data$reaction_id)
  unique_carbons <- unique(ess_data$Abb)
  
  # Create a binary matrix (Carbon x Reaction)
  # Initialize with zeros
  binary_mat <- matrix(0, 
                       nrow = length(unique_carbons), 
                       ncol = length(unique_reactions),
                       dimnames = list(unique_carbons, unique_reactions))
  
  # Fill the matrix: Set 1 if the reaction is essential for that carbon source
  for (carbon in unique_carbons) {
    active_rxns <- ess_data$reaction_id[ess_data$Abb == carbon]
    binary_mat[carbon, colnames(binary_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Calculate pairwise Manhattan distances between carbon sources
  dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(binary_mat, method = "manhattan"))
  
  # Convert to long format for easier merging
  dist_df <- reshape2::melt(dist_mat)
  colnames(dist_df) <- c("carbon1", "carbon2", paste0("rxndiff_", strain_id))
  
  return(dist_df)
}

# Define filenames and corresponding strain names
model_files <- c("iML1515__essential_only.csv", "ECOR11__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR31__essential_only.csv", "ECOR32__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR38__essential_only.csv", "ECOR50__essential_only.csv",
                 "ECOR55__essential_only.csv", "ECOR71__essential_only.csv")

strain_names <- c("MG1655", "ECOR11", "ECOR31", "ECOR32", "ECOR38", "ECOR50", "ECOR55", "ECOR71")

# Iteratively load data and merge into a single dataframe
combined_dist_df <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files)) {
  temp_dist <- calculate_gem_distances(model_files[i], strain_names[i])
  
  if (is.null(combined_dist_df)) {
    combined_dist_df <- temp_dist
  } else {
    combined_dist_df <- left_join(combined_dist_df, temp_dist, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))
  }
}

# Calculate median distance across all models (excluding the reference MG1655)
# This provides a robust representative metabolic distance
median_calculation_df <- combined_dist_df %>% select(-carbon1, -carbon2, -rxndiff_MG1655)
combined_dist_df$rxndiff_median <- apply(as.matrix(median_calculation_df), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

# Merge back with the primary carbon_pairs dataset
carbon_pairs_pre_cols <- colnames(carbon_pairs_pre)
carbon_pairs_updated <- left_join(carbon_pairs_pre, combined_dist_df, by = c("carbon1", "carbon2"))

## --- Visualization: Correlation between models ---
# Plot a pair-panel to check consistency of metabolic distances across different models
# Only using 'upper' triangle pairs to avoid redundancy
carbon_pairs_updated %>%
  filter(key == "upper") %>%
  select(starts_with("rxndiff_")) %>%
  psych::pairs.panels(method = "spearman", 
                      line.col = "red", 
                      pch = 21, 
                      main = "Consistency of Metabolic Distances across GEMs")

# Finalize the carbon_pairs dataframe for subsequent analysis
carbon_pairs <- carbon_pairs_updated %>%
  select(all_of(carbon_pairs_pre_cols), rxndiff_median, rxndiff_MG1655)

Sys.time()
```

## 1.4 Construction of the integrated essential reaction matrix (Supplementary Data)
```{r Carbon4}
# Function to generate a binary essentiality matrix for a specific GEM
generate_essential_matrix <- function(csv_filename, strain_id) {
  # Load carbon abbreviation mapping
  carbon_map <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "growth_media","Abb_carbon.csv"))
  
  # Load raw essentiality data
  raw_data <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "FBA", "output", "essential_by_species", csv_filename))
  
  # Join and filter valid carbon sources
  processed_data <- raw_data %>%
    left_join(carbon_map, by = "carbon") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Abb))
  
  # Get unique reactions and carbons to define matrix dimensions
  unique_rxns <- unique(processed_data$reaction_id)
  unique_abbs <- unique(processed_data$Abb)
  
  # Initialize the binary matrix with zeros
  # Using strain_id as a grouping column for the final integrated table
  essential_mat <- matrix(0, 
                          nrow = length(unique_abbs), 
                          ncol = length(unique_rxns),
                          dimnames = list(unique_abbs, unique_rxns))
  
  # Fill the matrix (1: Essential, 0: Non-essential)
  for (carbon in unique_abbs) {
    active_rxns <- processed_data$reaction_id[processed_data$Abb == carbon]
    essential_mat[carbon, colnames(essential_mat) %in% active_rxns] <- 1
  }
  
  # Convert to a dataframe and add strain identification
  essential_df <- as.data.frame(essential_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("carbon_name") %>%
    mutate(strain = strain_id) %>%
    select(strain, carbon_name, everything())
  
  return(essential_df)
}

# Integrate all models into a single master matrix
integrated_ess_mat <- NULL

for (i in seq_along(model_files)) {
  temp_df <- generate_essential_matrix(model_files[i], strain_names[i])
  
  if (is.null(integrated_ess_mat)) {
    integrated_ess_mat <- temp_df
  } else {
    # bind_rows automatically handles cases where reaction sets (columns) differ between models,
    # filling missing entries with NA.
    integrated_ess_mat <- bind_rows(integrated_ess_mat, temp_df)
  }
}

# Handle NAs: Reactions absent in a specific model are treated as non-essential (0)
# This ensures a complete binary matrix for the supplementary material
integrated_ess_mat[is.na(integrated_ess_mat)] <- 0

# Define carbon sources to exclude from global statistics
excluded_carbons <- qw(Glu, Ser, Cit, Arg, His, Lys, Thr, Arab)

# Final output object
ess_rxn_mat_all <- integrated_ess_mat %>% 
  filter(carbon_name %nin% excluded_carbons)

Sys.time()
```
## 1.5 Clustering carbon sources based on the consensus of 7 ECOR GEMs
```{r Carbon5,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=9,dpi=300}
# Prepare the distance matrix using the median metabolic distance
carbon_matrix_7gem <- carbon_pairs %>%
  filter(!is.na(rxndiff_median)) %>%
  select(carbon1, carbon2, rxndiff_median) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon2, values_from = rxndiff_median) %>%
  column_to_rownames("carbon1") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Sorting for consistency
target_order <- sort(rownames(carbon_matrix_7gem))
carbon_matrix_7gem <- carbon_matrix_7gem[target_order, target_order]

# Convert to distance matrix object
carbon_dist_matrix_7gem <- as.dist(carbon_matrix_7gem)


# Perform hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
# This consensus clustering represents the average metabolic relationships across E. coli diversity
carbon_row_cluster_7gem <- hclust(carbon_dist_matrix_7gem, method = "ward.D2")

# Extract ordered labels and join with metabolic category metadata for coloring
carbon_labels_ordered_7gem <- data.frame(label=carbon_row_cluster_7gem$labels[carbon_row_cluster_7gem$order])
carbon_labels_ordered_7gem<-left_join(carbon_labels_ordered_7gem,carbon_names,by=c("label"="Abb"))

## --- Visualization: Consensus Dendrogram ---
dend_sbst_7gem<-as.dendrogram(carbon_row_cluster_7gem)

## --- Visualization: Consensus Dendrogram ---
dend_7gem <- as.dendrogram(carbon_row_cluster_7gem)

# Customize appearance: labels colored by metabolic category
dend_7gem <- dend_7gem %>% 
  set("labels_cex", 1.5) %>% 
  set("labels_colors", carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category_col) %>%
  set("branches_lwd", 5)

# Plot the dendrogram
plot(dend_7gem, 
     main = "Clustering based on Median Metabolic Distance (7 ECOR GEMs)",
     ylab = "Median Manhattan Distance")

Sys.time()
```
## 1.6 Venn Diagram: Overlap of Essential Reactions
```{r Carbon6, fig.height=3, fig.width=3, dpi=300}
# Define representative carbon sources
carbon_reps <- qw(Glc, Succ, Lac)

# Filter the integrated essential reaction matrix for a specific strain (e.g., ECOR11)
# Transform to long format to identify presence/absence of each reaction
ess_rxn_long <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain == "ECOR11" & carbon_name %in% carbon_reps) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(strain, carbon_name), names_to = "rxn", values_to = "is_essential")

# Create a list where each element contains the names of essential reactions for that carbon source
venn_list <- list(
  Glc= ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Glc" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1],
  Succ = ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Succ" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1],
  Lac = ess_rxn_long$rxn[ess_rxn_long$carbon_name == "Lac" & ess_rxn_long$is_essential == 1]
)

# Generate the Venn diagram
# Note: venn.diagram returns a gList object that needs to be drawn via grid.draw
venn_plot <- venn.diagram(
  x = venn_list,
  filename = NULL,         # Do not save to file, return as an object
  disable.logging = TRUE,  # Suppress log files in the working directory
  fill = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#E69F00"), # Colors for Glc, Succ, Lac
  alpha = 0.6,             # Transparency for overlapping regions
  lty = "blank",           # Remove borders for a cleaner look
  cat.cex = 1.2,           # Category label size
  cex = 1.2,               # Numerical label size
  main = "Essential Reaction Overlap (ECOR11)"
)

# Draw the Venn diagram using the grid package
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(venn_plot)

# Data Inspection: Identify reactions essential for Glucose but NOT for Succinate
# Using basic set logic (setdiff) which is standard in R
glc_unique_to_succ <- setdiff(venn_list$Glucose, venn_list$Succinate)
print("Reactions essential for Glucose but not for Succinate:")
print(glc_unique_to_succ)

Sys.time()

```
## 1.7 Summary Statistics of Essential Reactions
```{r Carbon7}
# Define carbon sources to exclude from global statistics
excluded_carbons <- qw(Glu, Ser, Cit, Arg, His, Lys, Thr, Arab)

# Filter dataset: Focus on 7 ECOR strains and representative carbon sources
ess_stats_mat <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain != "MG1655" & !(carbon_name %in% excluded_carbons)) %>% 
  select(-strain, -carbon_name) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# 1. Distribution of the number of essential reactions per condition
# (Each row represents a specific strain on a specific carbon source)
essential_counts <- rowSums(ess_stats_mat)
print("Summary of the number of essential reactions per condition:")
print(summary(essential_counts))

# 2. Number of "Core" essential reactions
# Reactions that are essential across ALL tested strains and ALL carbon sources
# Using colAlls from matrixStats for efficiency, or a simple logical check
core_reactions_n <- sum(colSums(ess_stats_mat) == nrow(ess_stats_mat))
cat("# of core reactions (essential in all conditions):", core_reactions_n, "\n")

# 3. Number of "Pan" essential reactions
# Reactions that are essential in at least ONE condition (strain or carbon source)
pan_reactions_n <- sum(colSums(ess_stats_mat) > 0)
cat("# of pan reactions (essential in at least one condition):", pan_reactions_n, "\n")

# 4. List of carbon sources included in this statistical summary
included_carbons <- ess_rxn_mat_all %>% 
  filter(strain != "MG1655" & !(carbon_name %in% excluded_carbons)) %>% 
  pull(carbon_name) %>% 
  unique()

print("Carbon sources analyzed in this summary:")
print(included_carbons)

Sys.time()
```



# 2 Phylogenetic tree of ECOR
## 2.1 Strain typing based on alignmrernt of core genome sequnces using Pansnp
### 2.1.1 load phylogenetic relationship based on core-genome SNP typing using Parsnp
```{r Phylogeny1}
## for Parsnp: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4262987/
## for EzClermont: https://github.com/nickp60/EzClermont/tree/master/docs/analysis

# Metadata validation and cleanup
ez_metadata <- read_csv(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "validation_metadata.csv")) %>%
  mutate(simple = gsub("(.*?) (.*)", "\\1", reported_phylogroup)) %>%
  select(-dataset, -reported_phylogroup) %>%
  filter(accession != "")

# Load ezClermont results
ez_expdata <- read_delim(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "2020-04-09-ezclermont.txt"), 
                         col_names = c("long_acc", "ezClermont_phylogroup")) %>%
  mutate(accession = gsub(".scaffold.fasta", "", 
                          gsub("(GCA_.*?\\.\\d)_(.*)", "\\1", long_acc)))

# Merge and validate consistency between reported and predicted phylogroups
ez_together <- left_join(ez_metadata, ez_expdata %>% select(-long_acc), by = "accession") %>%
  mutate(raw_match = (simple == ezClermont_phylogroup))

# Correct known mismatches for specific Clades/Cryptic lineages
ez_together <- ez_together %>%
  mutate(match = ifelse(grepl("Clade", simple) & grepl("cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup) & !raw_match, 
                        TRUE, raw_match))

# Load ClermontTyping results for comparison
ez_expdata_ct <- read_delim(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "2020-04-09-CT-results.txt"), 
                            col_names = c("accession", "alleles", "profile", "al", "ct_phylotype", "mashpath")) %>%
  mutate(accession = gsub(".scaffold.fasta", "", gsub("(.*?\\..)_(.*)", "\\1", accession)),
         ct_phylotype = gsub("(.*?) (.*)", "\\1", ct_phylotype)) %>%
  select(accession, ct_phylotype)

ez_together <- left_join(ez_together, ez_expdata_ct, by = "accession")

# 2.1.2 Phylogenetic Tree Construction and Visualization
# Load the Maximum Likelihood tree (Parsnp output)
ez_tree <- ape::read.tree(file.path(getwd(), "EzClermont", "parsnp.clean.phy_phyml_tree.txt"))

# Standardize tip labels to match accession formats
ez_tree$tip.label <- ifelse(!startsWith(ez_tree$tip.label, "0"),
                            paste0("ESC_", ez_tree$tip.label),
                            paste0("GCA_", ez_tree$tip.label))

# Prepare label dataframe for ggtree mapping
labdf <- data.frame(label = ez_tree$tip.label, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(ez_together %>% mutate(label = substr(accession, 1, 13)), by = "label") %>%
  mutate(
    label2 = ifelse(match, strain, paste0("(", ezClermont_phylogroup, ") ", strain)),
    # Consolidate cryptic clades for visualization
    quardiplex_pcr_base_tidy = ifelse(grepl("lade", simple), "Cryptic", simple),
    ct_phylotype = ifelse(grepl("lade", ct_phylotype), "Cryptic", 
                          ifelse(grepl("Unknown", ct_phylotype), "U", ct_phylotype)),
    ezClermont_phylogroup = ifelse(grepl("cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup), "Cryptic", ezClermont_phylogroup)
  )

# Define Phylogroup Color Palette
colors <- c(A="grey", B1="darkgreen", B2="purple", C="orange", 
            "Clade I"="yellow", "Cryptic"="yellow", "Clade II"="yellow", 
            "Clade IV"="yellow", "Clade V"="yellow", D="red", E="green", 
            F="steelblue", G="black", U="pink")

# Visualization: Circular tree with heatmaps and phylogroup highlights
tp <- gheatmap(
  ggtree(ape::root.phylo(ez_tree, node = 142), layout = "circular", branch.length = 'none') %<+% labdf +
    geom_hilight(node = 145, fill = colors['A'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 179, fill = colors['B1'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 218, fill = colors['B2'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 199, fill = colors['C'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 212, fill = colors['D'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 202, fill = colors['E'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 135, fill = colors['F'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hilight(node = 132, fill = colors['G'], alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_tiplab2(aes(label = label2), size = 3, offset = 5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "right"),
  data = labdf %>% select(label, Reported = quardiplex_pcr_base_tidy, ClermonTyping = ct_phylotype, EzClermont = ezClermont_phylogroup) %>%
    column_to_rownames("label"),
  colnames_position = "top", width = 0.2, font.size = 2
) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors)+ labs(fill="Phylogroup")
print(tp)


# 2.1.3 ECOR-specific Subtree Generation
# Filter for ECOR and K12-MG1655 strains
labdf_sub <- labdf %>% 
  filter(grepl("^ECOR", strain) | strain == "K12-MG1655") %>%
  rename(Phylogroup = ezClermont_phylogroup)

# Manual curation for specific strains (based on literature: doi:10.1099/acmi.0.000143)
labdf_sub$Phylogroup[labdf_sub$strain %in% c("ECOR44", "ECOR49")] <- "D"

# Extract and plot the subtree
sub_tree <- ape::keep.tip(ez_tree, labdf_sub$label)

# ggtree(sub_tree, layout="circular", branch.length="none") + geom_text(aes(label=node))
ggtree(sub_tree, layout = "circular") %<+% labdf_sub +
  geom_tiplab2(aes(label = strain), size = 3, offset = 0.001) +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = Phylogroup), size = 2) +
  geom_hilight(node = 84, fill = pgPalette['A'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 108, fill = pgPalette['B1'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 131, fill = pgPalette['B2'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 121, fill = pgPalette['C'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 126, fill = pgPalette['D'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 123, fill = pgPalette['E'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hilight(node = 76, fill = pgPalette['F'], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_treescale(x = 0.006, y = 71, offset = 1) +
  labs(title = "Phylogeny of ECOR strains and MG1655") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Update
labdf_sub<-labdf_sub %>% 
  filter(grepl("^ECOR", strain)) # remove K12-MG1655

Sys.time()
```
### 2.1.2 Transforming Phylogenetic Distance Matrix to Long-format Dataframe
```{r Phylogeny2}
# 1. Compute pairwise distances between tips based on the branch lengths (ML tree)
# cophenetic.phylo calculates the sum of the edge lengths between each pair of tips
phylo_dist_mat <- cophenetic.phylo(sub_tree)

# 2. Map accession labels back to strain names for better readability
# Ensure the mapping matches the current matrix order
strain_mapping <- labdf_sub$strain[match(rownames(phylo_dist_mat), labdf_sub$label)]
rownames(phylo_dist_mat) <- colnames(phylo_dist_mat) <- strain_mapping

# 3. Filter for ECOR strains only to create a focused distance matrix
ecor_indices <- grep("^ECOR", rownames(phylo_dist_mat))
phylo_dist_mat <- phylo_dist_mat[ecor_indices, ecor_indices]

# 4. Identify matrix positions (Upper triangle, Lower triangle, or Diagonal)
# This tagging is essential for downstream correlation analyses to avoid redundant pairs
n_strains <- nrow(phylo_dist_mat)
pos_tag_mat <- matrix("upper", n_strains, n_strains)
pos_tag_mat[lower.tri(pos_tag_mat)] <- "lower"
diag(pos_tag_mat) <- "diag"

# 5. Convert the distance matrix to a long-format dataframe
phylo_dist_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(phylo_dist_mat))
colnames(phylo_dist_df) <- c("strain1", "strain2", "phylo_dist")

# 6. Append the positional tags (flattening the tag matrix in the same order)
phylo_dist_df$Type  <- as.vector(pos_tag_mat)

# 7. Data Inspection
# Review the first few rows to ensure correct mapping
print("Preview of the phylogenetic distance dataframe:")
head(phylo_dist_df)
Sys.time()
```

```{r MA1,fig.height=10,fig.width=5, dpi=300}
dat<-paste(getwd(),"From_RawOD_to_GrowthProf","Output","stat_fit_ma.csv",sep="/") %>% read_csv()
```

## 3.2 Variance in growth rate across MA lineage
```{r MA2,fig.height=10,fig.width=5.5, dpi=300}
carbon<-dat$carbon %>% unique()
n_carbon<-carbon %>% length()
lineage<-dat$lineage %>% unique()
n_lineage<-lineage %>% length()
round<-dat$round %>% unique()
n_round<-round %>% unique()
anc_colony<-dat$Anc %>% unique()


i<-1
j<-1
for (i in 1:n_carbon){
  my_carbon<-carbon[i]
  my_dat<-dat[dat$carbon==my_carbon,]
  my_dat[(my_dat$lineage %nin% c("lineage1","lineage5","lineage9"))&
           (my_dat$round==0),]$mu_max<-NA #<- remove overlapped anc data (use Anc data of lineages 1, 5, 9)
  my_df<-data.frame(round=round,carbon=my_carbon,mean_mu=NA,sd_mu=NA,var_mu=NA)
  for (j in 1:nrow(my_df)){
    my_round<-my_df$round[j]
    my_df$mean_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$sd_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% sd(na.rm = TRUE)
    my_df$var_mu[j]<-my_dat[my_dat$round==my_round,]$mu_max %>% var(na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  if(i==1){
    stat_df<-my_df
  }else{
    stat_df<-bind_rows(stat_df,my_df)
  }
}
stat_df$cv_mu<-stat_df$sd_mu/stat_df$mean_mu

g<-ggline(stat_df,x="round",y="cv_mu",numeric.x.axis = TRUE, alpha=0.5,ylab="Coefficient of variation [arb. unit]")
g<-ggpar(g, font.y = c(14, "black"))
facet(g,facet.by = "carbon")

g<-ggline(stat_df,x="round",y="var_mu",numeric.x.axis = TRUE, alpha=0.5)
facet(g,facet.by = "carbon")
Sys.time()
```
## 3.3 Calc relative growth rate to anc (rel growth rate)
```{r MA3}
gr_ma_df<-dat
gr_ma_df$rel_mu_max<-NA
i<-1
j<-1
for(i in 1:length(carbon)){
  my_carbon<-carbon[i]
  for(j in 1:length(anc_colony)){
    my_anc<-anc_colony[j]
    my_gr_anc<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
                       (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc)&
                       (gr_ma_df$round==0),]$mu_max %>% unique()
    gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&
            (gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$rel_mu_max<-gr_ma_df[(gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon)&(gr_ma_df$Anc==my_anc),]$mu_max/my_gr_anc
  }
}
Sys.time()
```

### 3.5.2 Relationship between metabolic pathway distance and evolutionary correlation
```{r MA6,fig.height=3,fig.width=5, dpi=300}
ma_pair_all<-carbon_pairs
ma_pair_all<-ma_pair_all[(ma_pair_all$carbon1 %in% ma_carbons)&(ma_pair_all$carbon2 %in% ma_carbons),]
ma_pair_all$correlation<-NA
i<-1
for (i in 1:nrow(ma_pair_all)){
  my_carbon_1<-ma_pair_all$carbon1[i]
  my_carbon_2<-ma_pair_all$carbon2[i]
  my_df1<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_1,]
  my_df1<-my_df1 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max)
  colnames(my_df1)[c(5,6)]<-qw(mu_max_1,rel_mu_max_1)
  my_df2<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$carbon==my_carbon_2,]
  my_df2<-my_df2 %>% select(carbon,Anc,lineage,round,mu_max,rel_mu_max)
  colnames(my_df2)[c(5,6)]<-qw(mu_max_2,rel_mu_max_2)
  my_df<-left_join(my_df1,my_df2,by=qw(Anc,lineage,round))
  my_df<-my_df[my_df$round>0,] #<------------------ Remove Anc
  my_res<-cor_test(my_df,vars = "rel_mu_max_1",vars2 = "rel_mu_max_2",method = "spearman")
  ma_pair_all$correlation[i]<-my_res$cor
}
```

### 3.6.3 Comparison with metabolic pathway distance in MA
#### 3.6.3.1 Entanglement score with permutation test in MA
```{r MA13, fig.width=1.5,fig.height=3.5,dpi=300}
# Genetic distance from FBA (7 GEMs consensus) and Phenotypic distance from Growth rates
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix)
# dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_pre[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 7 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Untangle: Optimize the layout of the two dendrograms to minimize crossings
# Maintaining the topology while rotating branches for better visualization
dl <- dendlist(dend_theory, dend_exp)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized Growth-based dendrogram


# 3. Create color vectors based on labels
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) dendrogram
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)
# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered_7gem$label)]

# 4. Set label colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match Growth-based tree labels with the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram
# Visualizing the structural similarity between metabolic theory and growth phenotype
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 1.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement indicates higher structural similarity
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fixed theory-based labels
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Calculate entanglement for the shuffled pair after untangling
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# P-value = Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Visualization of results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 3.6.3.1 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test in MA
```{r MA14}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms
dist_exp<-as.dist(1 - ma_matrix)
my_ins<-rownames(ma_matrix)

# Theoretical distance based on 7 GEMs consensus
# dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_pre[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ iML1515
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix_7gem[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist() # <------ 7 GEMs

# Hierarchical clustering
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This measures how well the tree structure reflects the original distance matrix
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Permutation Test for Cophenetic Correlation ---
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Get original labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while keeping the underlying matrix structure intact
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Convert to matrix to reassign shuffled names
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = "ward.D2")
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Calculate and store the correlation for this permutation
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Proportion of permutations where correlation is equal to or greater than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') # 各座標の重複数をカウント

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Plotting with ggscatter
# Bubble size and color intensity are log2-scaled to visualize the density of distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map count to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map count to fill color
          color = "black",          # Fix border color to black
          shape = 21,               # Use filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to size and color to handle the wide range of counts
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)

Sys.time()
```

### 4.4.1 Evolutionary correlation for each of three clusters defined by hieralchical clustering
```{r ECOR10,fig.width=2,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
# 1. Clustering based on experimental evolutionary distances
# Define the number of theoretical clusters (k)
k_val <- 3

dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Create a mapping table for carbon sources and their assigned clusters
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)

# Print carbon sources belonging to each cluster for inspection
for(i in 1:k_val){
  paste("cluster ",i,": ",paste(my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==i,]$carbon,collapse = ","),sep="") %>% print()
}

# 2. Data Integration
# Focus on unique pairs (upper triangle) and join with cluster assignments
my_df<-ecor_pair_all[ecor_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)

# 3. Iterative Comparison: Within-cluster vs. Between-cluster Correlations
my_list<-list()
my_p_list<-list()
for(i in 1:length(my_clstrs)){
  my_cls<-my_clstrs[i]
  
  # Select pairs where at least one carbon source belongs to the target cluster
  my_dat<-my_df[(my_df$exp1==my_cls)|(my_df$exp2==my_cls),]
  n_cbn<-my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==my_cls,] %>% nrow()
  
  # Perform analysis only if the cluster contains more than one carbon source
  if(n_cbn>1){
    # Label pairs as either "Within" (the specific cluster number) or "Between"
    my_dat$pair_cluster_exp<-"Between"
    my_dat[my_dat$exp1==my_dat$exp2,]$pair_cluster_exp<-as.character(my_cls)
    
    # Set factor levels for consistent plotting order
    my_dat$pair_cluster_exp<-factor(my_dat$pair_cluster_exp,levels=c(as.character(my_cls), "Between"))
    
    # 4. Visualization: Boxplot with Jitter
    # Comparing evolutionary correlations within the cluster vs. with others
    my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,
            x="pair_cluster_exp",y="correlation",
            ylab="Evolutionary correlation [arb. unit]",xlab="",
            add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
            # palette = my_palette,
            legend="")+
    stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
             ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
      p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1.2))
    
    # 5. Statistical Testing: Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test
    my_res<-my_dat %>%
      wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_cluster_exp,
      ref.group = "Between",
      p.adjust.method = "BH")
    my_p_list[[i]]<-my_res$p
  }
}

# 6. Global P-value adjustment across all cluster comparisons
p_adjusted_all <- p.adjust(unlist(my_p_list), method = "BH")
print("Adjusted P-values for all clusters:")
print(p_adjusted_all)

# Output individual plots
my_list[[1]]
my_list[[2]]
my_list[[3]]

Sys.time()
```

### 4.5.3 Entanglement score with permutation test in ECOR (processing time: 15 min)
```{r ECOR13, fig.width=1.8,fig.height=5,dpi=300}
# 1. Pre-processing: Create initial dendrograms
# Genetic distance (FBA theory) and Evolutionary distance (ECOR data)
dend_fba_raw <- as.dendrogram(carbon_row_cluster)
current_labels <- labels(dend_fba_raw)

# Color labels based on metabolic categories
dend_fba_raw <- dend_fba_raw %>% 
  set("labels_colors", carbon_labels_ordered$Category_col)

dend_ecor_raw<- as.dendrogram(ecor_row_cluster)

# 2. Untangle: Minimize crossing lines between the two dendrograms
# This optimizes the visualization without changing the underlying topology
dl <- dendlist(dend_fba_raw, dend_ecor_raw)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] # Optimized FBA-based dendrogram
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] # Optimized ECOR-based dendrogram

# 3. Create color vectors for plotting
# Retrieve current label order from the left (FBA) tree
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)

# Map categories and colors to the current labels
groups_p <- carbon_labels_ordered$Category[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered$label)]
col_vector_p <- carbon_labels_ordered$Category_col[match(current_labels_p, carbon_labels_ordered$label)]

# 4. Set label colors (branches remain black)
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# Match labels of the ECOR-based tree to the FBA-based tree's color vector
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram for ECOR
# Assessing structural similarity between metabolic theory and natural evolution
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE, 
           color_lines = col_vector_p, # Connecting lines match category colors
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 2.5, 4),  # Narrow central column to emphasize links
           margin_inner = 3.5,          
           margin_outer = 0.5,             
           # 枝の色を黒で固定
           axes = FALSE)

# legend
# legend("topleft", legend = names(pgPalette), fill = pgPalette, title = "Phylogroup", cex = 0.8)


# 6. Calculate Observed Entanglement Score
# Lower entanglement score suggests higher similarity between trees
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

print(Sys.time())

# 7. Permutation Test for Entanglement
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Fix the structural layout of the theoretical tree
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Create a copy of the experimental dendrogram and shuffle labels
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Perform untangle for each shuffle to maintain consistency with the observed value
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 8. Calculate P-value
# P-value: Probability that random entanglement is lower than the observed value
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 9. Results Visualization
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))
Sys.time()
```

### 4.5.4 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test in ECOR
```{r ECOR14}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
dist_theory<-carbon_dist_matrix
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
# This evaluates the correlation between the dendrogram-induced distances and original matrices
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Integrated Permutation Test ---
# Generating a null distribution by shuffling labels to evaluate statistical significance
print(Sys.time())
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Retrieve labels (strain names) from the experimental distance matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle only the labels while maintaining the distance matrix structure
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Re-assign shuffled labels to the matrix
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct the dendrogram from the shuffled distance matrix
  # Consistency in the clustering method (ward.D2) is crucial
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = "ward.D2")
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Compute and store correlation for the permuted pair
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
  
  # Progress monitoring
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Probability of obtaining a correlation as high as observed by chance
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping distance pairs for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Visualization using ggscatter
# Point size and color intensity are log2-scaled to reflect the density of identical distance pairs
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",          # Map number of ties to dot size
          fill = "count",           # Map number of ties to color intensity
          color = "black",          # Solid black borders for bubbles
          shape = 21,               # Filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to handle the wide range of point densities
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt)

Sys.time()
```
### 4.5.5 Baker's Gamma Index for Topological Similarity
```{r ECOR15}
# 1. Prepare distance matrices and initial dendrograms for ECOR
dist_theory<-carbon_dist_matrix
dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2 method
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# 2. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# Baker's Gamma measures the rank correlation between the stages at which 
# pairs of objects combine in each dendrogram.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_theory, dend_exp)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 3. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Building a null distribution by randomly shuffling labels to assess significance
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly shuffle the labels of one dendrogram while preserving its structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_theory, replace = FALSE)
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the shuffled pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_exp)
}

# 4. Calculate P-value
# P-value: The probability of obtaining a Gamma value as high as observed by chance
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
```

```{r ECOR17,fig.width=2,fig.height=3,dpi=300}
}
```

```{r ECOR18, fig.width=1.8,fig.height=2.5,dpi=300}
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram for the subset (Excluding Upper Glycolysis)
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "FBA-based",
           main_right = "Growth-based",
           lab.cex = 1,
           lwd=2,
           columns_width = c(4, 2.5, 4),
           margin_inner = 3.5,
           margin_outer = 0.5,
           axes = FALSE)


# 6. Permutation Test for Entanglement Score
# Evaluating the statistical significance of the topological similarity in the subset
actual_ent <- entanglement(dl_untangled) # Entanglement score after untangling

set.seed(123)
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
perm_ent <- numeric(n_perm)

# Shuffling labels while keeping the structural layout of the theoretical tree fixed
labels_theory <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  shuffled_dend <- dend_t
  labels(shuffled_dend) <- sample(labels_theory)
  
  # Standardize by applying untangle to each permuted pair
  perm_dends <- dendlist(dend_p, shuffled_dend) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  perm_ent[i] <- entanglement(perm_dends)
  
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Calculate P-value
# Lower entanglement score reflects higher similarity
p_val_ent <- sum(perm_ent <= actual_ent) / n_perm

# 8. Plot Results
hist(perm_ent, main="Permutation Test for Entanglement", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", xlim=c(0, 1))
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2)
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement: %.3f\nP-value: %.4f\n", actual_ent, p_val_ent))

Sys.time()
```
#### 4.5.6.2 Cophenetic correlation with permutation test
```{r ECOR19}
# 1. Data Preparation: Subsetting carbon sources for Cophenetic Correlation
# Excluding 'Upper Glycolysis' to test the robustness of the metabolic constraints
mat_exp<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
# my_rows<-paste("ECOR",sprintf("%02d", mat_exp$strain),sep="")
my_rows<-mat_exp$strain
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(-strain)

# Filter carbon sources based on category
my_ins<-carbon_labels_ordered[carbon_labels_ordered$Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis",]$label
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(all_of(my_ins)) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(mat_exp)<-my_rows

# Calculate distances for the subset
dist_exp<-mat_exp %>% spearman_dist()
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist()

# Hierarchical clustering using Ward's D2
hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

# dend_theory <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(dist_theory))) # Placeholder for structure check
dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)

# Calculate observed Cophenetic correlation (Spearman)
actual_cor <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_exp, method = "spearman")

# --- Integrated Permutation Test ---
# Generating null distribution to evaluate statistical significance of the correlation
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_results <- data.frame(cor = numeric(n_perm))

# Retrieve labels (strain names) from the subset experimental matrix
exp_labels <- rownames(as.matrix(dist_exp))

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # 1. Shuffle labels while maintaining the underlying distance structure
  dist_shuffled <- dist_exp
  shuffled_labels <- sample(exp_labels)
  
  # Re-assign shuffled names to the distance matrix
  temp_mat <- as.matrix(dist_shuffled)
  rownames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  colnames(temp_mat) <- shuffled_labels
  
  # 2. Reconstruct dendrogram from the shuffled matrix
  hc_shuffled <- hclust(as.dist(temp_mat), method = "ward.D2")
  dend_shuffled <- as.dendrogram(hc_shuffled)
  
  # 3. Compute and store correlation for the permuted pair
  perm_results$cor[i] <- cor_cophenetic(dend_theory, dend_shuffled, method = "spearman")
}

# --- Statistical Evaluation ---
# P-value: Probability that random correlation is equal to or higher than observed
p_val_cor <- sum(perm_results$cor >= actual_cor) / n_perm

cat("【Analysis Results: Subset without Upper Glycolysis】\n")
cat(sprintf("Cophenetic Cor (Spearman): %.3f (p = %.4f)\n", actual_cor, p_val_cor))

# --- Visualization: Cophenetic Correlation Bubble Plot ---
# 1. Prepare data and count overlapping points (ties) for bubble sizing
df_coph <- data.frame(
  Theory = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_theory)),
  Experiment = as.vector(cophenetic(hc_exp))
) %>%
  group_by(Theory, Experiment) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') 

my_txt<-paste("R=",sprintf("%.3f",actual_cor),sep="")

# 2. Visualization with ggscatter
# Point size and fill color reflect the density of identical distance pairs (log2-scaled)
ggscatter(df_coph, x = "Theory", y = "Experiment",
          size = "count",           # Map overlap count to bubble size
          fill = "count",           # Map overlap count to fill intensity
          color = "black",          # Solid black borders
          shape = 21,               # Filled circles with borders
          alpha= 0.8,
          xlab = "Cophenetic distance (Theory)",
          ylab = "Cophenetic distance (Experiment)",
          title = "Cophenetic Correlation (Log-scaled Bubble Size)",
          ylim=c(0,3)) +
  # Apply log2 transformation to optimize visualization of overlapping points
  scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 12), name = "Count (log2)") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", trans = "log2", direction = 1, name = "Count (log2)")+
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 2.7, label = my_txt,)
Sys.time()
```
#### 4.5.6.3 Baker's Gamma Index (Subset without Upper Glycolysis)
```{r ECOR20}
# 1. Data Preparation: Subsetting carbon sources for Topological Comparison
# Excluding Upper Glycolysis to evaluate the robustness of tree structure similarity
mat_exp<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
# my_rows<-paste("ECOR",sprintf("%02d", mat_exp$strain),sep="")
my_rows<-mat_exp$strain
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(-strain)

# Filter for the specific subset of carbon sources
my_ins<-carbon_labels_ordered[carbon_labels_ordered$Category %nin% "Upper Glycolysis",]$label
mat_exp<-mat_exp %>% select(all_of(my_ins)) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(mat_exp)<-my_rows

# Compute distances and build dendrograms
dist_exp<-mat_exp %>% spearman_dist()
dist_theory<-carbon_matrix[my_ins,my_ins] %>% as.dist()

hc_theory <- hclust(dist_theory, method = "ward.D2")
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")

dend_theory <- as.dendrogram(hc_theory)
dend_exp    <- as.dendrogram(hc_exp)


# 2. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# This index assesses the rank correlation of the stages where pairs of carbon sources merge
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_theory, dend_exp)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 3. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Assessing if the topological similarity is significantly higher than random expectation
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Randomly shuffle labels while maintaining the dendrogram's branching structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_theory, replace = FALSE)
  # Calculate Baker's Gamma for the permuted pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_exp)
}

# 4. P-value Calculation
# Proportion of random permutations with Gamma equal to or greater than observed
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))
```

### 4.6.5 Phylogenetic signals
#### 4.6.5.1 Kmult (multi variate)
```{r ECOR26}
my_tmp <- gr_ecor_df
# my_tmp$strain <- paste("ECOR", sprintf("%02d", my_tmp$strain), sep = "")
my_tmp <- my_tmp %>% pivot_wider(names_from = carbon, values_from = mu_max)

ecor_mlsubtree <- sub_tree
my_df <- data.frame(label = ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label)
my_df <- left_join(my_df, labdf_sub, by = "label")
ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label <- my_df$strain
ecor_mlsubtree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, my_tmp$strain)

ecor_physig_mat <- my_tmp %>% select(-strain) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(ecor_physig_mat) <- my_tmp$strain
ecor_physig_mat <- ecor_physig_mat[ecor_mlsubtree$tip.label, ]

# Replace branches of length 1e-08 or 0 with a small computable value (e.g., 1e-06)
ecor_mlsubtree$edge.length[ecor_mlsubtree$edge.length < 1e-6] <- 1e-6

k_mult_result <- physignal(ecor_physig_mat, ecor_mlsubtree, iter = 999)
print(summary(k_mult_result)) 

# 1. Standardize the data (mean = 0, variance = 1 for each column)
ecor_physig_mat_scaled <- scale(ecor_physig_mat)

# 2. Recompute the multivariate phylogenetic signal
# * Use 'ecor_mlsubtree' whose branch lengths were adjusted to 1e-06 above
mult_signal_scaled <- physignal(A = ecor_physig_mat_scaled, phy = ecor_mlsubtree, iter = 999)

# 3. Display the results
summary(mult_signal_scaled)
Sys.time()
```

#### 4.6.5.2 Pagel's lambda
```{r ECOR27, fig.height=3,fig.width=5, dpi=300 }
# Create a container to store results for each environment
# env_names <- colnames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled)
env_names <- colnames(ecor_physig_mat)
results_list <- data.frame(Environment = env_names, Lambda = NA, P_val = NA)

# Loop through each environment and compute Pagel's lambda
for(i in 1:length(env_names)) {
  env_data <- ecor_physig_mat_scaled[, i]
  names(env_data) <- rownames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled)
  
  # Remove missing values if present
  clean_data <- env_data[!is.na(env_data)]
  current_tree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, names(clean_data))
  
  # Compute Pagel's lambda
  sig <- phylosig(current_tree, clean_data, method = "lambda", test = TRUE)
  
  results_list$Lambda[i] <- sig$lambda
  results_list$P_val[i] <- sig$P
}

# Multiple testing correction using Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method
results_list$P_adj <- p.adjust(results_list$P_val, method = "BH")

# Show significant environments
print(results_list[results_list$P_adj < 0.05, ])


base_val <- 0.00001
p<-ggplot(results_list, aes(x = Environment, y = Lambda)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) - 0.4,

  scale_y_log10(limits = c(base_val, 10),
```

#### 4.6.5.3 Blomberg's K
```{r ECOR28, fig.height=3,fig.width=5, dpi=300 }
# 1. Phylogenetic Signal Estimation using Blomberg's K
# Initialize a data frame to store K-statistics and P-values for each environment (carbon source)
k_results <- data.frame(Environment = env_names, K_stat = NA, P_val = NA)

for(i in 1:length(env_names)) {
  # Extract scaled growth data for the current environment
  env_data <- ecor_physig_mat_scaled[, i]
  names(env_data) <- rownames(ecor_physig_mat_scaled)
  
  # Remove missing values (NA) to ensure tree-data compatibility
  clean_data <- env_data[!is.na(env_data)]
  # Prune the ML subtree to match the available phenotypic data
  current_tree <- keep.tip(ecor_mlsubtree, names(clean_data))
  
  # Compute Blomberg's K with 999 permutations to assess significance
  sig_k <- phylosig(current_tree, clean_data, method = "K", test = TRUE, nsim = 999)
  
  k_results$K_stat[i] <- sig_k$K
  k_results$P_val[i] <- sig_k$P
}

# 2. Statistical Correction
# Apply Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment for multiple testing across environments
k_results$P_adj <- p.adjust(k_results$P_val, method = "BH")

# Display significant environments (where phylogenetic signal is detected)
print("Significant Phylogenetic Signals (BH-adjusted P < 0.05):")
print(k_results[k_results$P_adj < 0.05, ])

ggbarplot(k_results,x="Environment",y="K_stat",fill="grey50",size=0)+
  scale_y_log10(
    limits = c(0.001, NA),      
    breaks = log_breaks(n = 5), 
    labels = label_log()       
  )+
  rotate_x_text(angle=90)

k_results$log_K <- log10(k_results$K_stat)

# 3. Visualization: Log-scaled Bar Plot for Blomberg's K
# Set the baseline for the log plot (K=1 represents the Brownian Motion expectation)
base_val <- 0.001
p<-ggplot(k_results, aes(x = Environment, y = K_stat)) +
  # Using geom_rect to precisely control the base of bars on a log-scale
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) - 0.4, 
                xmax = as.numeric(as.factor(Environment)) + 0.4, 
                ymin = base_val, 
                ymax = K_stat), 
            fill = "grey50") +
  # Configure log10 scale with appropriate breaks and labels
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(base_val, 10), 
                breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x), 
    labels = label_log())+                              
  # Horizontal line at K = 1 (Standard Brownian Motion model)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1)+
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(y = "Blomberg's K [arb. unit]")+
  rotate_x_text(angle = 90)
ggpar(p,xlab="")

Sys.time()
```
### 4.6.6 Entanglement analysis between phylogeny and growth-based dendrogram
#### 4.6.6.1 Entanglement score with permutation test
```{r ECOR29, fig.width=5,fig.height=4}
# 1. Pre-processing: Ultrametric tree conversion and dendrogram creation
# Convert the ML tree to an ultrametric tree (equal root-to-tip distances)
tree_ultra <- chronos(ecor_mlsubtree)
dend_p_raw <- as.dendrogram(as.hclust(tree_ultra))

# Compute phenotypic distance based on Spearman correlation of growth profiles
dist_trait <- as.dist(1 - cor(t(ecor_physig_mat), method = "spearman"))
dend_t_raw <- as.dendrogram(hclust(dist_trait, method = "ward.D2"))

# 2. Untangle: Optimize branch rotation for visualization
# Minimizing line crossings while strictly maintaining the topology of both trees
dl <- dendlist(dend_p_raw, dend_t_raw)
dl_untangled <- dendextend::untangle(dl, method = "step2side")

dend_p <- dl_untangled[[1]] 
dend_t <- dl_untangled[[2]] 

# 3. Color mapping based on Phylogroups
# Retrieve labels in the current optimized order from the phylogeny (left tree)
current_labels_p <- labels(dend_p)

# Map labels to their respective Phylogroups and assign colors from pgPalette
groups_p <- labdf_sub$Phylogroup[match(current_labels_p, labdf_sub$strain)]
col_vector_p <- pgPalette[groups_p]

# Align trait tree label colors with the phylogeny colors
dend_p <- dend_p %>% set("labels_colors", col_vector_p)

# 4. Set label colors (branches remain neutral black)
dend_t <- dend_t %>% 
  set("labels_colors", col_vector_p[match(labels(dend_t), current_labels_p)])

# 5. Draw Tanglegram: Phylogeny vs. Growth Traits
tanglegram(dend_p, dend_t,
           common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, 
           highlight_distinct_edges = FALSE,
           highlight_branches_lwd = FALSE,         
           color_lines = col_vector_p, 
           main_left = "Phylogeny",
           main_right = "Trait-based",
           lab.cex = 0.4,
           columns_width = c(5, 5, 5), 
           margin_inner = 4,           
           margin_outer = 1,             
           axes = FALSE)
# legend("topleft", legend = names(pgPalette), fill = pgPalette, title = "Phylogroup", cex = 0.8)

# Calculate the observed entanglement score after untangling
actual_ent<-dendextend::entanglement(dend_p, dend_t) # Entanglement score
cat(sprintf("Actual Entanglement (after untangle): %.3f\n", actual_ent))

# 6. Permutation Test for Significance
# Assessing if the topological similarity is better than random expectation
n_perm <- if_else(iteration_scale=="large",1000,10)
null_entanglements <- numeric(n_perm)

cat("Starting permutation test (this may take a while)...\n")
print(Sys.time())

set.seed(123) 
labels_fixed <- labels(dend_p)

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Copy the trait tree and shuffle its labels
  dend_shuffled <- dend_t
  labels(dend_shuffled) <- sample(labels_fixed)
  
  # Re-run untangle for each shuffle to create a fair null distribution
  dl_perm <- dendlist(dend_p, dend_shuffled) %>% 
    dendextend::untangle(method = "step2side")
  
  # Record optimized entanglement for the null model
  null_entanglements[i] <- dendextend::entanglement(dl_perm)
  
  if(i %% 100 == 0) cat(sprintf("Iteration %d/%d completed\n", i, n_perm))
}

# 7. Statistical Evaluation (P-value)
# Proportion of shuffled trees that achieved a score as low as the actual data
p_value <- sum(null_entanglements <= actual_ent) / (n_perm + 1)

# 8. Plot the Null Distribution
print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

hist(null_entanglements, 
     main="Permutation Test (with untangle)", 
     xlab="Entanglement Score", 
     xlim=c(0, 1), col="lightgray")
abline(v = actual_ent, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend=c("Actual Score"), col="red", lwd=2, lty=2)
```

### 4.6.7 Baker's Gamma Index for Phylogeny-Trait Congruence
```{r ECOR31}
# 1. Calculate Observed Baker's Gamma Index
# This measures the rank correlation between the merging stages of the Phylogeny 
# and the Trait-based dendrograms.
actual_gamma <- cor_bakers_gamma(dend_p, dend_t)
cat(sprintf("Actual Baker's Gammer: %.3f\n", actual_gamma))

# 2. Permutation Test (1,000 iterations)
# Assessing the significance of the topological similarity by shuffling labels
set.seed(123)
n_perm <- 1000
perm_gammas <- numeric(n_perm)

# Progress tracking for larger permutations
cat("Calculating null distribution for Baker's Gamma...\n")

for(i in 1:n_perm) {
  # Shuffle the labels of the phylogeny dendrogram while preserving its branching structure
  perm_dend <- sample.dendrogram(dend_p, replace = FALSE)
  
  # Compute Baker's Gamma for the permuted pair
  perm_gammas[i] <- cor_bakers_gamma(perm_dend, dend_t)
}

# 3. P-value Calculation
# P-value: The probability that a random label assignment would yield 
# a Baker's Gamma equal to or higher than the observed value.
p_value <- sum(perm_gammas >= actual_gamma) / n_perm

print(Sys.time())
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

# 4. Result Interpretation
if(p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("The topological similarity between phylogeny and traits is statistically significant.\n")
} else {
  cat("No significant topological similarity was detected between phylogeny and traits.\n")
}

```

## 5.3 Evolutionary correlation of MA across clusters defined by ECOR
```{r MA_and_ECOR3,fig.width=1.6,fig.height=2,dpi=300}
# 1. Cluster Definition based on ECOR (Natural Evolution)
# Setting the number of clusters (k) to partition the ECOR growth-based tree
k_val <- 3

dist_exp<-ecor_dist_matrix
hc_exp    <- hclust(dist_exp, method = "ward.D2")
cluster_exp    <- cutree(hc_exp, k = k_val)

# Mapping ECOR clusters to carbon sources used in the MA experiments
my_tmp<-data.frame(carbon=names(cluster_exp),exp=cluster_exp)
my_tmp<-my_tmp[my_tmp$carbon %in% ma_carbons,]

# 2. Data Integration for MA Pairwise Correlations
# Filter for unique pairs from MA results and map their corresponding ECOR clusters
my_df<-ma_pair_all[ma_pair_all$key=="upper",]
my_tmp1<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon1=carbon,exp1=exp)
my_tmp2<-my_tmp %>% rename(carbon2=carbon,exp2=exp)
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp1,by="carbon1")
my_df<-left_join(my_df,my_tmp2,by="carbon2")

# 3. Statistical Comparison: Within-ECOR-Cluster vs. Between-Cluster in MA Data
# Testing if natural evolutionary modules predict short-term mutational coherence
my_clstrs<-seq(1,k_val)
my_list<-list()
my_p_list<-list()
for(i in 1:length(my_clstrs)){
  my_cls<-my_clstrs[i]
  
  # Select MA pairs where at least one member belongs to the current ECOR cluster
  my_dat<-my_df[(my_df$exp1==my_cls)|(my_df$exp2==my_cls),]
  
  # Ensure the cluster has multiple members to allow within-cluster comparison
  n_cbn<-my_tmp[my_tmp$exp==my_cls,] %>% nrow()
  if(n_cbn>1){
    my_dat$pair_cluster_exp<-"Between"
    # Identify pairs where both members are within the same ECOR cluster
    mmbr_clst<-my_dat[my_dat$exp1==my_dat$exp2,] %>% nrow()
    if(mmbr_clst>0){
      my_dat[my_dat$exp1 == my_dat$exp2, ]$pair_cluster_exp <- as.character(my_cls)
      my_dat$pair_cluster_exp <- factor(my_dat$pair_cluster_exp, levels = c(as.character(my_cls), "Between"))
      
      # 4. Visualization: Boxplot with Wilcoxon Test
      my_list[[i]]<-ggboxplot(my_dat,
        x="pair_cluster_exp",y="correlation",
        ylab="Evolutionary correlation [arb. unit]",xlab="",
        add="jitter",add.params = list(alpha=0.5),
        # palette = my_palette,
        legend="")+
        # Pairwise comparison against the "Between" group baseline
        stat_pwc(method = "wilcox.test",label = "p.adj.signif",
               ref.group = "Between",tip.length = 0,
        p.adjust.method = "BH",hide.ns = TRUE)+
        scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.8, by = 0.4), limits = c(-0.4, 1))
      
      # 5. Formal Wilcoxon test and store P-values for global BH correction
      my_res<-my_dat %>%
        wilcox_test(formula = correlation ~ pair_cluster_exp,
        ref.group = "Between",
        p.adjust.method = "BH")
      my_p_list[[i]]<-my_res$p
    }
  }
}

# 6. Global Multiple Testing Correction
# Adjusting P-values across all tested clusters
p_adj_summary <- p.adjust(my_p_list %>% unlist(), method = "BH")
print("Adjusted P-values for each ECOR cluster comparison:")
print(p_adj_summary)

# Display comparisons for each cluster
my_list[[1]]
my_list[[2]]
my_list[[3]]

Sys.time()


```



# 6 PCA
## 6.1 ECOR and MA
```{r PCA1,fig.height=2.5,fig.width=2.5}
# Define common carbon sources between MA and ECOR
carbons_ecorma_common<-ma_carbons[ma_carbons %in% ecor_carbons]
carbons_ecorma_common<-carbons_ecorma_common[order(carbons_ecorma_common)]

# A (ECOR)
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = mu_max)
my_rows<-paste("ECOR",gr_ecor_com_mat$strain,sep="_")
gr_ecor_com_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ecor_com_mat)<-my_rows
A_mat<-gr_ecor_com_mat

# B (MA)
## Anc
gr_ma_anc_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round==0,] %>% distinct(carbon,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_anc_df$name<-"MA_Anc@0"
## Offspring
gr_ma_offsp_df<-gr_ma_df[gr_ma_df$round!=0,] %>% select(lineage,round,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_offsp_df$name<-paste(gr_ma_offsp_df$lineage,sprintf("%02d", gr_ma_offsp_df$round),sep="@R")
## Anc & Offspring
gr_ma_com_mat<-bind_rows(gr_ma_anc_df,gr_ma_offsp_df) %>% select(name,carbon,rel_mu_max)
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat%>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carbon,values_from = rel_mu_max)
my_rows<-gr_ma_com_mat$name
my_rows<-my_rows %>% str_replace_all(pattern = "lineage",replacement = "L")
gr_ma_com_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat %>% select(carbons_ecorma_common) %>% as.matrix()
rownames(gr_ma_com_mat)<-my_rows
B_mat<-gr_ma_com_mat


# 1. Normalization
A_scaled <- scale(A_mat) # ECOR
B_scaled <- scale(B_mat) # MA

# 2. Extract principal components of (co-)variation across carbon sources
## 2.1. PCA for dataset B
pca_B <- prcomp(B_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
## 2.2. PCA for dataset A
pca_A <- prcomp(A_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Calc. variance explained
## 3.1. for dataset B 
var_B_own <- pca_B$sdev^2 / sum(pca_B$sdev^2) # ratio of total variance
cum_B_own <- cumsum(var_B_own) # cumulative variance
## 3.2. for dataset A
var_A_own <- pca_A$sdev^2 / sum(pca_A$sdev^2)
cum_A_own <- cumsum(var_A_own)

# 4. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_summary <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(var_B_own),
  Variance = var_B_own,
  Cumulative = cum_B_own
)

# 5. Project A onto the principal component space of B
# Apply the principal component axis (rotation matrix) of B to A_scaled
# A_projected represents principal score (coordinates) of A in B's PC space.
A_projected <- scale(A_mat,center = pca_B$center,scale = pca_B$scale) %*% pca_B$rotation
var_A_on_B <- apply(A_projected, 2, var)
var_explained_A_on_B <- var_A_on_B / sum(var_A_on_B)
cum_A_on_B <- cumsum(var_explained_A_on_B)

# 6. Generate a dataframe for visualization
pca_compare <- data.frame(
  PC = rep(1:length(var_B_own), 2),
  Variance = c(var_B_own, var_explained_A_on_B),
  Cumulative = c(cum_B_own, cum_A_on_B),
  Type = rep(c("MA", "ECOR"), each = length(var_B_own))
)

# dataset B: MA
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_B, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()
# dataset A: ECOR
fviz_pca_biplot(pca_A, repel = TRUE, col.var = "red", col.ind = "grey50",labelsize = 2,arrowsize=0.3)+
  theme_pubr()


#
pc_map<-data.frame(
  PC1=c(pca_B$x[,1],A_projected[,1]),
  PC2=c(pca_B$x[,2],A_projected[,2]),
  PC3=c(pca_B$x[,3],A_projected[,3]),
  Type=c(rep("MA",nrow(pca_B$x)),rep("ECOR",nrow(A_projected))),
  Name=c(rownames(pca_B$x),rownames(A_projected))
)
ggscatter(pc_map[pc_map$Type=="MA",],x="PC1",y="PC2",
          # repel = TRUE,label = "Name",font.label = c(6),
          color="#00BFC4",legend.title="",alpha=0.9)


Sys.time()
```

## 6.2 random dataset
```{r PCA2}
# 1. Settings
n_row <- nrow(gr_ecor_com_mat); n_col <- length(carbons_ecorma_common)
#set.seed(123)
# B_rnd_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n_row * n_col), nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col)
# B_rnd_scaled <- scale(B_rnd_mat)
# pca_B_rnd <- prcomp(B_rnd_scaled, scale. = TRUE)

# 2. Generate random datasets 10,000 times
n_sim <- 1000
sim_results <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_sim, ncol = n_col)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
  # A_rnd_mat
  A_rnd_tmp <- matrix(rnorm(n_row * n_col), nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col)
  # Normalize using the parameters from dataset B (MA)
  A_rnd_scaled <- scale(A_rnd_tmp, center = pca_B$center, scale = pca_B$scale)
  A_rnd_proj <- A_rnd_scaled %*% pca_B$rotation
  
  # Compute cumulative explained variance
  vars <- apply(A_rnd_proj, 2, var)
  sim_results[i, ] <- cumsum(vars) / sum(vars)
}

# 3. Compute summary statistics (mean, 2.5th percentile, 97.5th percentile)
stats_rand_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:n_col,
  Mean = colMeans(sim_results),
  Lower = apply(sim_results, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
  Upper = apply(sim_results, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
)

# 4. Visualization
ggplot(stats_rand_df, aes(x = PC, y = Mean)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1/n_col, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") + # Theoretical uniform line
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:n_col) +
  labs(title = "Cumulative Proportion of Variance (10,000 Iterations)",
       subtitle = "Projecting Random A onto PCA space of Random B",
       x = "Principal Component (of Dataset B)",
       y = "Cumulative Proportion") +
  theme_pubr()
```
